title: How a Zipper Works in 60 Seconds 🤐🧥 #shorts
description:
The modern zipper was designed in 1913, and it still works the same way. Each tooth has a small bump on top and a matching hollow underneath. A Y-shaped channel inside the slider squeezes the teeth together at an angle, so they interlock like tiny hooks, and a wedge inside pushes them apart again. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#zipper #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: The modern zipper was designed back in *1913*, and it still works the exact same way.

steps.label: Teeth
steps.text: Each tooth has a small *bump* on top, and a matching *hollow* underneath.

steps.label: Slider
steps.text: The *slider* hides a Y-shaped channel. Two openings at the top, one at the bottom.

steps.label: Close
steps.text: Pull it up, and the channel squeezes the teeth together at an angle, so each bump *snaps* into the next hollow.

steps.label: Lock
steps.text: Now the teeth *interlock* like tiny hooks. Pulling the fabric sideways can't separate them.

steps.label: Open
steps.text: Pull down, and a *wedge* inside the slider pries the teeth apart, one by one.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Bump, hollow, *slide*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
